name: WCOTW World Championship
epitaph: No dated title-history ledger survives for this belt. Buff won it from Undertaker at Halloween Havoc (25 Oct 1998, by internal dating; the show's own winner call does not use explicit "new champion" language the way sibling title matches on the same card did, but the match is explicitly billed for the title). The fed's own dated 1998 weekly-show logs and PPV recaps otherwise show the belt changing hands repeatedly across its run (among others, HBK, Goldberg, Ravishing Rob Reynolds, Agent-X, Mystik, Buff, and Da Don are each attested as champion at some point). Its own last surviving snapshot (undated, ~2001) names Cold Blooded Mike Bauce champion, with no document recording the change between.

name: WCOTW US Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: No dated title-history ledger survives for this belt. Cold Blooded Mike Bauce was already billed champion entering Halloween Havoc (25 Oct 1998, by internal dating) and retained there against The Canadian Crippler; the fed's own last surviving snapshot (undated, ~2001) instead names Mystik champion, with no document recording the change between.

name: WCOTW Can-Am Championship
epitaph: Krypt is the only holder this belt's surviving record ever names — already billed champion entering Halloween Havoc (25 Oct 1998, by internal dating), retaining there against Taz, and still attested champion on the fed's own last surviving snapshot (undated, ~2001). No dated title-history ledger survives, but the two attestations bracket a single continuous reign.

name: WCOTW Television Championship
epitaph: Brett Clark won this title from defending champion Casper in an Inferno Match at Halloween Havoc (25 Oct 1998, by internal dating), setting Casper on fire for the finish. The fed's own last surviving snapshot (undated, ~2001) instead names Krypt champion, with no document recording the change between.

name: WCOTW European Championship
epitaph: Saturn won this title from Warrior at Halloween Havoc (25 Oct 1998, by internal dating) — neither wrestler is billed champion in the match's own ring introduction, so only the title change itself is confirmed, not who held it before. Saturn is still the attested champion on the fed's own last surviving snapshot (undated, ~2001), bracketing the held record's single longest-attested WCOTW reign of any title.
